hints: Think about what type of alcohol LiAlH4 can actually make from a carboxylic acid, primary, secondary or tertiary?
Carboxylic acid reduction always gives a primary alcohol with the $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ group, so W must not be primary.
Now compare the two remaining secondary alcohols and ask how many different alkenes each can form on loss of water.
walkthrough:
**Use the LiAlH4 clue first**

Great start is to remember what LiAlH4 does. It reduces a carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol only.

Chemical rule:
$$\text{RCOOH} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{RCH}_2\text{OH (primary alcohol only)}$$

**Eliminate the primary alcohols**

Since W cannot be made this way, W cannot be primary. It must be secondary or tertiary.

Check the list: $\text{butan-1-ol}$ ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) is primary, and $\text{propan-1-ol}$ ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) is primary. Both can be made from their acids, so both are out.

**Use the dehydration clue**

Dehydration with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ removes $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to form an alkene. If there is more than one possible position for the double bond, you get more than one product.

$$\text{butan-2-ol} \rightarrow \text{but-1-ene} + \text{but-2-ene (two products)}$$
$$\text{propan-2-ol} \rightarrow \text{propene only (one product)}$$

**Pick the alcohol that fits both clues**

Only propan-2-ol is non-primary and gives a single alkene, propene, because the molecule is symmetrical. That matches both conditions perfectly.

options.A: Butan-1-ol is a primary alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. It can be made by reducing butanoic acid with LiAlH4, so it fails the first condition. It does dehydrate to only but-1-ene, but that is not enough.
options.B: Butan-2-ol is secondary, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, so it correctly cannot be made from a carboxylic acid. However, dehydration can remove H from C1 to give but-1-ene or from C3 to give but-2-ene, so it gives two products and fails the second condition.
options.C: Propan-1-ol is a primary alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. It can be made by reducing propanoic acid with LiAlH4, so it fails the first condition. Students sometimes pick it because it dehydrates to only propene, but both conditions must be met.
options.D: Propan-2-ol is secondary, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, so it cannot be formed by LiAlH4 reduction of a carboxylic acid. On dehydration, loss of water can only give $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$ (propene) because both sides of the molecule are identical, so only one product forms. It fits both clues.
